''Superkruiken'' (Super Pitchers) | founded = {{start date and age|df=yes|1896|8|12}} (as ''Tilburgia'') | ground = [[Koning Willem II Stadion]] | capacity = 15,220 | chairman = Meindert van Duijvenbode | mgrtitle = Head coach | manager = [[John Stegeman]] | league = {{Dutch football updater|Willem II}} | season = {{Dutch football updater|Willem II2}} | position = {{Dutch football updater|Willem II3}} | current = 2026–27 Willem II Tilburg season | pattern_la1 = _willemii2627h | pattern_b1 = _willemii2627h | pattern_ra1 = _willemii2627h | pattern_sh1 = _willemii2627h | pattern_so1 = _willemii2627hl | leftarm1 = FFFFFF | body1 = FFFFFF | rightarm1 = FFFFFF | shorts1 = FFFFFF | socks1 = FFFFFF | pattern_la2 = | pattern_b2 = | pattern_ra2 = | pattern_sh2 = | pattern_so2 = | leftarm2 = | body2 = | rightarm2 = | shorts2 = | socks2 = | pattern_la3 = | pattern_b3 = | pattern_ra3 = | pattern_sh3 = | pattern_so3 = | leftarm3 = | body3 = | rightarm3 = | shorts3 = | socks3 = | website = {{URL|https://www.willem-ii.nl/}} }} '''Willem II Tilburg''' ({{IPA|nl|ˈʋɪləm ˈtʋeː}}), commonly known simply as '''Willem II''', is a Dutch [[football club (association football)|football club]] based in [[Tilburg]], Netherlands. They play in the [[Eredivisie]], the top tier of [[Dutch football league system|Dutch football]], following promotion from the [[Eerste Divisie]] via the [[2025–26_Eerste_Divisie#Promotion/relegation_play-offs|2025–26 promotion/relegation play-offs]]. The club was founded on 12 August 1896 as ''Tilburgia''. On 12 January 1898, the club was renamed ''Willem II'' after [[List of Dutch monarchs|Dutch king]] [[William II of the Netherlands|William II]] (1792–1849), who, as Prince of [[House of Orange-Nassau|Orange]] and commander of the [[Royal Netherlands Army|Dutch army]], had his military headquarters in Tilburg during the [[Belgian Revolution|Belgian uprising of 1830]], spent much time in the city after becoming king, and died there.{{cite web |title=Historisch Overzicht |url=http://www.willem-ii.nl/Willem-II/Club/Historisch-overzicht.aspx |website=Willem-ii.nl |access-date=30 January 2017 |archive-date=10 May 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170510183652/http://www.willem-ii.nl/Willem-II/Club/Historisch-overzicht.aspx |url-status=dead }} Notable former players for the club include Dutch internationals [[Jan van Roessel]], [[Joris Mathijsen]], [[Jaap Stam]], [[Frenkie de Jong]], [[Marc Overmars]], [[Virgil Van Dijk]] and Finland's [[Sami Hyypiä]]. The club's shirt consists of red-white-blue vertical stripes, inspired by the colours of the [[flag of the Netherlands]]. Willem II plays its home matches in the [[Koning Willem II Stadion]], also named after the King. The stadium, opened on 31 May 1995, has a capacity of 14,700 spectators. The average attendance in 2004–05 was 12,500 people. The club has won the [[Eredivisie]] three times, and the [[Eerste Divisie]] four times."}}
